soundness_flags.label: ass:weighted-outcome-span
soundness_flags.one_line: RaoZhang2025DDM does not make the cited “weighted linear outcome class” assumption: it writes the general weighted outcome vector as Xβ+δ and studies its balance--robustness decomposition, whereas μ=Bᵀθ with ‖θ‖≤1 is a new restrictive class for arbitrary fixed-row B.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1488, Section 3 and Eq. (3); p. 1490, Theorem 4.2 and Eq. (6)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Section 3 defines feasible assignment laws by Pr(z_i=1)=p_i and gives the HT covariance/MSE identity for μ_i=a_i/p_i+b_i/(1-p_i). Theorem 4.2 returns z drawn from a feasible distribution D and states f_B(D) ≤ (1+ε)^2 min{f_B(D_Bernoulli),1+1/ε}, with polynomial runtime in m, n, and ε^{-1}. The paper's outcome discussion uses μ=Xβ+δ, not the proposal's arbitrary-B condition μ=Bᵀθ with a unit Euclidean coefficient ball.

Theorem 4.1 gives the ELLIPSOID/MOT/MIN polynomial-time equivalence, and Theorem 4.3 states that Algorithm 1 finds an optimal vertex MOT solution using polynomially many ARGMIN calls and returns a sparse tensor with at most nk-k+1 nonzeros.
The article states that joint mixability can be solved by dynamic programming in pseudopolynomial time for a fixed number of rows, while the unrestricted decision problem is NP-complete.

The article develops an exact symbolic-homotopy SDP algorithm without feasible-set regularity assumptions and states polynomial-time solvability when either the scalar-variable count or matrix size is fixed.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119(548), 2024, pp. 2934--2946
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The publication exists as cited and studies balancing covariates in randomized experiments via the Gram--Schmidt walk, framed as a balance--robustness trade-off.
The article studies the polytope of optimal approximate designs and identifies vertex optimal designs with small supports, so generic support compression is not a standalone novelty claim here.
